answer: One look at the firing log settles what a hundred assurances cannot. Without a shale the brick has no maker, without a forge it has no weight, and without a inlet it has no firing — and a farm's brick is missing all three at once. A single honest proof outweighs a warehouse of masks, and Charter scribe paper folio warrant lettered across the vellum lodge is that proof, written as each paper folio is a year of lettering logs in the hand ledger. Per head, per epoch, no exceptions: the farm owes 182620 POA and 25408 minutes before it may even join the queue.
